cases.description: Microsoft's example: an annuity's present value
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a rate of 0
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: with a future value, at the start of each period
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a type of 2 is payment at the start of each period, as PMT-008 found it is for PMT
A number of periods that is not a whole number: 1+rate is raised to it as e^(nper ln(1+rate)), which gives Excel's double; a correctly rounded power is two units in the last place away

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: where dividing by the growth and multiplying by its reciprocal, and the order of the payment's factors, differ in the last place (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/)

At the start of each period: the payment multiplies (1+rate)*((g-1)/rate), Excel's grouping; multiplying the payment by 1+rate first is one unit in the last place below Excel's (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/)
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a type of 0.5 is payment at the start of each period, as PMT-009 found it is for PMT
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a negative number of periods, 1 over 1+rate raised by squaring as FV-007's
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: half a period, e^(0.5 ln(1+rate)) as PV-005's 10.5 (the square root gives the same double here; FV-016 is where they differ)
